summary: Dashboard attached threshold alerts not firing when panel uses custom bucketing / timezone alignment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that threshold alerts attached to a dashboard panel did not fire during multiple spikes visible in the panel. The panel uses a custom bucketing scheme (5m buckets) and the dashboard timezone set to Auto (detect from browser). The alerts are configured as simple threshold alerts (metric > 0.8) with evaluation window 10m and for: 2m.

Impact:
- Customer missed 3 alerting events over a 4 hour period on 2026-03-12 which they rely on to autoscale downstream services.
- Potential business impact: delayed incident response and over-provisioning while investigating.

Environment:
- Customer: ByteFrame Analytics (dedicated cluster, us-east region)
- Console version: web-frontend v2.11.3
- Alerting-service: alerts-api v1.9.7, evaluator v1.9.7
- Timeseries store: tsdb v3.4.2 (bucketed rollups enabled)

Steps to reproduce (customer-facing):
1) In their dedicated console, open a dashboard with a timeseries panel that uses 5m bucketing and dashboard timezone set to Auto.
2) Create a threshold alert on the panel: condition metric > 0.8, evaluation_window=10m, for=2m.
3) Wait for a metric spike that appears in the panel (they observed spikes at 08:05, 09:15, 11:40 UTC).
4) Observe that the panel shows the spike but no alert notification is generated.

Observed logs and artefacts provided by customer:
- Panel screenshot (attached in ticket) showing spike at 2026-03-12T09:15:00Z and no alert hit.
- Customer query history: query id q-20260312-9a4e
- Alert evaluation logs (from alerts-api):
  [2026-03-12T09:16:10Z] eval: alert_id=bf-73 rule=threshold eval_window=10m buckets=[2026-03-12T09:10:00Z,2026-03-12T09:15:00Z] result=NO_DATA
  [2026-03-12T09:16:11Z] query-engine: query_id=q-20260312-9a4e time_range=[2026-03-12T09:06:00Z-2026-03-12T09:16:00Z] buckets=5m returned_points=1
- Console audit log shows dashboard view at 2026-03-12T09:16:05Z using browser TZ=Europe/London (BST).

Notes: The customer provided a session replay and the timeline indicates the dashboard panel bucket visually aligned with the spike, but the alert evaluation considered an earlier set of bucket boundaries and returned NO_DATA for the expected buckets.

investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Reproduced with synthetic data on dedicated stack using same tsdb rollup config.
- alerts-evaluator evaluated time windows aligned to UTC bucket boundaries by default. When a dashboard/panel uses a non-UTC timezone or 'auto' browser TZ, the query-engine requests bucket boundaries shifted by local offset.
- This produced a 5-minute misalignment: evaluator checked buckets [09:10,09:15] while query-engine returned points for visual buckets [09:12,09:17] due to rollup bucket offseting logic.
- Logs show evaluator returned NO_DATA for the buckets it evaluated even though data existed in the shifted buckets.
Hypothesis: regression introduced in alerts-evaluator v1.9.4 where timezone offset was dropped when converting evaluation window to rollup-aligned boundaries.
Evidence: git bisect points to commit 7f2b1c2 in alerts-evaluator that changed window alignment code to use time.FixedZone incorrectly. Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1348
Telemetry: added debug logs for evaluator boundary calculation (enabled for customer's dedicated cluster) to capture future events.
resolution_notes:
Workaround (customer-facing):
- Short term: Set dashboard timezone to UTC for affected dashboards or change alert evaluation window to use a fixed lookback (e.g., evaluation_window=12m) so boundaries overlap with rollup buckets. We validated this prevented missed alerts for subsequent spikes.
- Medium term: Patch PR merged (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1348) that ensures evaluator uses tsdb bucket offset when calculating boundaries. Patch currently under canary rollout to staging and one dedicated customer cluster.
- Permanent fix: PR includes unit tests and adds an integration test that exercises non-UTC dashboard timezone with rollups. SRE to monitor canary for 48 hours before wider rollout.
Follow-ups / Action items:
- ENG-1592: Add end-to-end test in CI for timezone-aware alert evaluation (owner: Diego Morales).
- OPS-4021: Monitor alert hit-rate telemetry; create dashboard to surface sudden NO_DATA patterns after fix rollout (owner: Ethan Reed).
- CS-117: Inform customers in affected set and provide KB article describing workaround and expected rollout schedule (owner: Priya Shah).
Current status: Patch merged into main; canary rollout started 2026-03-14 05:00Z. Monitoring in progress.
public_resolution_summary: We identified a bug where alert evaluation windows were aligned to UTC bucket boundaries while the query path used dashboard-local bucket offsets. This caused alerts to evaluate empty buckets even when the dashboard showed data. We deployed a patch to ensure the evaluator respects TSDB rollup offsets and provided a temporary workaround (set dashboard timezone to UTC or increase evaluation_window). Canary rollout is in progress; full rollout pending 48h validation.
